GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2015-06-03T17:47:46Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: IP address as a url param error
Description: When declaring an IP address as a URL parameter `req.params` incorrectly parses the value. 

Add the following param to the URL  `:ip((?:[0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3})`

Use the value 192.168.1.2 for ip

Then check  `req.params.ip` it will return as 1. 

```
console.log('req.originalUrl',req.originalUrl);
console.log('(req.params.ip',req.params.ip);
```


You must provide a category number (1-3). Your response must follow this format exactly:

CATEGORY: [category number]
REASONING: [your reasoning here, including specific reasons why an issue would be hard to dockerize if choosing category 3]
llm_response:
CATEGORY: 2
REASONING: This issue requires a build environment to verify because we need to actually run Express.js code to see how it handles IP addresses as URL parameters. The issue describes a specific behavior where an IP address (192.168.1.2) in a URL parameter with a regex pattern is being incorrectly parsed as "1" in req.params.ip. To verify any solution, we would need to:

1. Set up an Express.js server
2. Configure routes with the specified parameter pattern
3. Make requests to that route with IP addresses
4. Check the actual output of req.params.ip

This is a runtime behavior issue that can't be verified through code analysis alone. However, this can be easily dockerized since it only requires a basic Node.js environment with Express.js installed, with no special hardware, network, or timing dependencies.
